newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT -T-bonds seek bounce to 107-15, then slide.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -T-bonds seek bounce to 107-15, then slide.

text.p: June T-bond futures continue to look negative but may see a slight move higher towards 107-15 on Monday before turning lower, technical analysts said.
"We expect at short term bounce for today, up towards 107-15, that's 38.2 percent of the slide from 108-11," said Elizabeth Miller, technical analyst at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
"If we got through there we'd see 107-24, but we don't favour that. We should see a short-term bounce and then we expect it to come off again."
At 0955 GMT, June T-bond futures were at 107-05 in automated trade, up one tick from Friday's Chicago settlement.
The market dropped from 108-11 to 106-31 from April 23 to April 25.
Miller said once the contract got down through 106-31, 106-12 would come into play and then there was the potential to get to 105-27.
She said 106-12 was the key level, being the low for this month, formed on April 11.
Stavros Loizou, manager of strategic trading desk at Fuji Bank in London, also said 106-12 was key support for T-bonds.
"Overall, having been to 106-31 on Friday, the market looks bleak," he said.
He said he was expecting a small bounce to be met with selling but that 106-23/24 would hold any decline.
On the upside, resistance was pegged at 107-09, a reaction level set on Thursday.
"There's not much above there until 107-28, 108-00 even," Loizou said.
Support was at 106-31 Friday's low, and then 106-23 which would fill an intraday gap, he said. Below there, 106-12 was the key level, the low set on April 11.
At the short end, September Eurodollars were unchanged at 93.670.
